turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How can you possibly imply that I am overstepping or taking an excessive interest in Mr. Wickham's affairs, when you are the one who has consistently shown a callous disregard for his well-being?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Elizabeth, that I am astonished by your audacity in questioning my motives, when it is you who has consistently shown a want of propriety and decorum in your behavior towards me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How dare you try to deflect and shift the blame onto me, when it is you who has been so flagrantly dishonest and cruel to me and others?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your accusations, Elizabeth, are as unfounded as they are unbecoming. I must insist that you retract your words and acknowledge the truth of my character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will not retract a single word, Mr. Darcy, for I know that my accusations are true and I will not be swayed by your attempts to intimidate me into silence.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your refusal to retract your words, Elizabeth, only serves to demonstrate your own lack of judgment and discernment.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I think it's clear that we have fundamentally different values and principles, Mr. Darcy, and I would never consider marrying someone who believes honesty and integrity are optional.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, I am astonished by the depth of your misunderstanding, Elizabeth. Your conviction in your own rectitude is admirable, but it blinds you to the truth of my character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I think it's time for you to acknowledge that your attempts to manipulate me into accepting your affections have been nothing short of insulting, Mr. Darcy.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must insist that your harsh judgments of my character are not only unjust, but also a grave misfortune for you, for you have misconstrued the very qualities that make me a superior gentleman.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I find it rich that you would lecture me on rectitude, Mr. Darcy, when your own behavior has consistently demonstrated a disregard for the feelings and rights of those around you.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your grand declarations of love, Mr. Darcy, when your actions have consistently demonstrated a lack of concern for the well-being and dignity of others.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your obstinacy, Elizabeth, is a reflection of your own prejudices and biases, rather than any genuine concern for the truth.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I suppose it's flattering that you think you could change my opinion of you with a few well-timed words, Mr. Darcy, but it won't work.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: You are blinded by your own vanity and prejudices, Elizabeth, and I fear that you will never be able to see me as I truly am.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I think it's time for you to acknowledge, Mr. Darcy, that your own behavior has been the subject of much discussion and criticism, and that your attempts to shift the blame onto me are nothing short of pathetic.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: You would do well to reflect on your own behavior, Elizabeth, rather than making baseless accusations against me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your condescension is wearing thin, Mr. Darcy. I'd rather not be lectured on my behavior by someone who has consistently demonstrated a lack of integrity.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am astonished that you would so callously dismiss my professions of love, Elizabeth, and that you would reduce them to a mere attempt to 'shift the blame' onto yourself.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I have no interest in hearing professions of love from someone who has spent years trying to manipulate and control those around him, Mr. Darcy.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Can you deny that you have done it?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: I have no wish of denying that I did everything in my power to separate my friend from your sister, or that I rejoice in my success. Towards him I have been kinder than towards myself.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
